Sam (AE): FYI - ACME PoC can't join trace spans from their frontend to our Console traces. They can see request lines but trace_id field is missing in Kibana and Datadog. Can SE + SRE help triage?
Rina (SE): On it. Quick question - are they using server-sent events (SSE) for streaming or plain HTTP chunked? SSE can cause some proxies to strip custom headers on upgrade.
Tom (SRE): Good call. Also check whether they're terminating TLS at CDN/edge (e.g., Fastly) which may rewrite headers.
Sam (AE): They mentioned Cloudflare in front and using fetch() streams from the browser.
Rina (SE): Browser cross-origin fetch won't send `X-Trace-Id` unless `access-control-expose-headers` is set and the header is allowed. Ask them to log the outgoing request headers from the browser console before send.
Helena (Platform Eng): Also verify our ingress doesn't treat `X-Trace-Id` as hop-by-hop. Intra-service proxies may drop headers that include hyphens in some configs.
Sam (AE): They pasted a browser network dump (trimmed): 
```
Request Headers: {
  "authorization": "Bearer REDACTED",
  "content-type": "application/json",
  "x-trace-id": "trace-12345",
  "origin": "https://app.acme.com"
}
```
Rina (SE): Looks fine from the client. Next, need a raw server-side access log line from our edge (nginx) showing all headers for that request. Sam - can you ask them to hit our `/v1/stream` with a curl that mirrors the browser and paste the ALB/nginx access log?
Sam (AE): Sent the curl snippet for them to run.
Rina (SE): Example curl to run: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Origin: https://app.acme.com" -H "X-Trace-Id: trace-12345" \ 
  -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Tom (SRE): If the header is present at our edge but missing in application logs, fluent-bit/json parser may be configured to pull `headers` from a nested `http.request` object. Ask for their Fluent Bit config.
Sam (AE): Customer pasted their Fluent Bit filter: 
```
[FILTER]
    Name record_modifier
    Match *
    Record trace_id ${http.request.headers.x-trace-id}
```
Rina (SE): That mapping won't work unless Fluent Bit's parser creates `http.request.headers` path. Recommend using `Lua` filter or `modify` with `Copy` after parsing. Suggest they try: 
```
[FILTER]
    Name modify
    Match *
    Copy http.request.headers.x-trace-id trace_id
```
Tom (SRE): Also, verify the collector isn't normalizing header names to lower-case or replacing hyphens with underscores. Datadog/ELK ingestion pipelines sometimes do that.
Helena (Platform Eng): I'm checking our ALB logs now. If Cloudflare is in front, CF can strip `Set-Cookie` and other headers on certain modes. We'll look at the request path.
ExportBot: telemetry-exporter: project-acme -> logging sink status: deployed, sink mapping: dd-forwarder, last-forward: 2026-03-22T01:05:00Z
Rina (SE): One more edge-case: when we stream SSE, the initial CONNECT/upgrade path may carry headers but subsequent payload frames are not per-request headers; ensure their tracer attaches the trace id to each logical chunk (or we attach `trace_id` to the request log at entry).
Sam (AE): They also saw some 429s in load tests, and those error responses often lacked trace_id. Could rate-limiter middleware short-circuit before header capture?
Tom (SRE): Yes - middleware ordering matters. If rate-limit returns a 429 from an early middleware, it must copy request headers into the error log entry. We'll check the middleware chain for `rateLimiter -> auth -> handler`. If rateLimiter sits first, it needs header passthrough.
Rina (SE): For quick repro, we asked them to run the curl above while we tail ingress and app logs. I'm enabling a temporary debug logger for the `acme-trial` tenant to print `req.headers` at entry.
Tom (SRE): I'll also enable a short-lived trace sampling of 100% for that tenant for 15 minutes so traces are generated regardless of their sampler.
Sam (AE): They also have questions about retaining trace logs in our Console for 30 days vs 90 days and the cost. Any guidance to give right now?
Helena (Platform Eng): High-level: retention is an add-on billed by storage (GB/month). Short answer for SQ: we store traces encrypted at rest, access logged, and retention can be configured per-tenant. I'll pull exact pricing from finance and attach.
Sam (AE): They asked if trace_id values could be mapped back to user emails. Need a short security blurb.
Rina (SE): Short answer: trace_id itself is opaque and doesn't contain PII. We scrub headers and mask values that match email patterns before storing. We'll provide the logging policy snippet.
ExportBot: exporter-health: dd-forwarder for project-acme -> healthy (last 5m).
Rina (SE): Next steps: 1) Sam to get curl + raw edge access log. 2) Customer to confirm Cloudflare passthrough settings and CORS expose headers. 3) Tom to monitor ingress and enable debug. 4) Helena to verify sink mapping and ingestion pipeline. 5) Rina to validate Fluent Bit mapping or provide a temporary Lua snippet.
Sam (AE): Scheduling a troubleshooting window tomorrow 9am PT. I'll attach the runbook and security blurb to the SQ response.
Tom (SRE): If we confirm header present at edge but missing in ingestion, we update runbook and roll a small fix to make sure `trace_id` is copied to error logs for 429s.
Rina (SE): Closing note: if they want an immediate workaround, they can send trace id in the request body or as a query param (less preferable) which bypasses header passthrough issues.
Sam (AE): Thanks all. I'll sync with the customer and post the results here. :white_check_mark:
